opening.greeting: Good morning, Vito. Let's process the boards.

weather.insight: Clear operating window. Good day to front-load external meetings and site movement.

opening.verse_of_the_day: This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it! — Psalms 118:24

market: JCI slipped 0.12% to 6,343.71, while US benchmarks closed flat with minimal losses.
KOSPI's 4.58% plunge and Hang Seng's 1.49% drop signal regional tech risk-off for Jakarta.
economic: BI rate steady at 5.75%, but US 10Y yield jumped to 4.67%, raising funding costs.
Rupiah firmed slightly to 17,914, yet Brent's 1% gain and record copper support exporters.
tech_ai: Google's AI-first search redesign and DeepMind leadership shift signal accelerating AI integration.
Railway's $100M AI-native cloud funding intensifies competition against AWS, impacting SEA tech.
political: Prabowo ordered faster power outage handling and fuel price stability, a domestic buffer.
US 15% tariff on polysilicon pressures China, potentially affecting regional supply chains.

arbiter_brief: US markets closed flat, offering no tailwind, while regional tech sell-offs—KOSPI down 4.58%—cap foreign inflows into Jakarta. The rupiah's slight firming is a rare positive, but the 10Y UST jump to 4.67% raises capital costs. Commodities counterbalance: Brent's gain and record copper, tied to Hormuz risk, bolster Indonesian exporters. Watch foreign net-selling if the dollar index holds above 100. Prabowo's stability directives provide domestic support but won't offset external tech de-rating. Stay defensive, favor commodity-linked cyclicals.
executive_brief: Prioritize commodity-linked cyclicals over growth; external tech de-rating caps Jakarta inflows.
Hedge against rising US yields; 10Y at 4.67% squeezes domestic project financing costs.
Monitor Hormuz escalation; Brent and copper gains underpin exporter earnings, but stay defensive.

sectors.name: Technology

Expect continued divergence between ID and US tech, favoring domestic plays on rupiah stability and government digitalization tailwinds.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in ABDA and BDMN on outsized volume; both are repricing on loan-growth and NIM resilience, but chase risk is high after 7-8% single-day pops. Rotate into PADI and NICK for laggard catch-up, as foreign flows favor mid-cap financials over banks. Trim ASMI into strength; its move is sentiment-driven, not fundamental.
themes: Indonesia's financial sector is decoupling from US rate swings, with domestic liquidity and loan demand driving a local beta that rewards mid-cap insurers and multi-finance names over big banks.
Regulatory tailwinds from OJK's digitalization push and MSME credit mandates are structurally lifting non-bank financials, making ABDA, BDMN, and PADI recurring outperformers.
Foreign ownership is rotating from US-listed financials into Jakarta-listed small/mid caps, creating persistent valuation gaps that close via M&A speculation and dividend hikes.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
sectors.ai: Buy the laggards: PTRO, APLI, and PH offer 7-8% upside on re-rating as foreign flows rotate into mid-cap infrastructure. BLES and RGAS are momentum traps—take profits. Position for Jokowi's final-term capex push and IKN-related logistics contracts; hold through Q3 earnings.
themes: Indonesia's new capital Nusantara (IKN) construction continues to drive demand for heavy equipment, logistics, and construction materials, benefiting mid-cap infrastructure names.
The government's accelerated infrastructure spending ahead of the 2024 election cycle supports order books for contractors and energy infrastructure firms, particularly in downstream oil and gas.
US rate-cut expectations are boosting risk appetite for emerging-market infrastructure equities, with foreign inflows favoring liquid, high-beta Indonesian names.

daily_brief.synthesis: Today's cross-market picture is mixed with a cautious undertone. Indonesia's IHSG slipped 0.12% to 6,343.71 despite Q2 GDP growth of 5.29%, as foreign investors bought big banks (BBCA, BMRI, BBRI) while the rupiah strengthened slightly to 17,914. US markets were dragged by tech losses (Nasdaq -0.06%, S&P -0.18%) amid rising Treasury yields (10Y +5.3bp to 4.67%) and oil price gains (Brent +1.02% to $83.33) on Middle East tensions, though a potential Iran-Oman Hormuz deal offers some optimism. Bitcoin fell 0.38% to $64,304. For Indonesia, the key is whether IHSG can hold support given global volatility and domestic resilience.

macro_analysis.point: Foreign investors are aggressively accumulating Indonesian large-cap banks (BBCA, BBRI, BMRI) despite a flat JCI, as seen in the news of 'Asing Borong Saham Bank Besar'. This rotation into high-liquidity financials is likely driven by attractive valuations and stable earnings, which supports the Rupiah (USD/IDR strengthened 0.10%) and underpins the JCI's resilience amid global tech weakness.

The sharp rise in US 10-year yields (+5.3 bp to 4.67%) and hawkish Fed commentary (Kashkari, Cook suggesting rate hikes) are pressuring global equities, especially tech-heavy indices like the Nasdaq and KOSPI (-4.58%). For Indonesia, this could dampen foreign flows into duration-sensitive tech and growth stocks, but the JCI's defensive tilt toward financials and consumer names may limit downside.

Commodity prices are firming: Brent crude rose 1.02% and copper hit record highs (per filtered signals), while Indonesian mining names like INCO (+0.46%) and the Mining & Energy sector (+0.49%) are outperforming. This is supportive for the Rupiah and Indonesia's commodity exporters, but rising oil prices could stoke imported inflation, complicating Bank Indonesia's rate stance.

The Rupiah's recent weakness (as discussed in CNBC Indonesia) is being countered by foreign inflows into banks, but the US dollar index is stable and US yields are rising. If the Fed hikes again, the Rupiah could face renewed depreciation pressure, forcing Bank Indonesia to defend the currency, potentially at the expense of domestic growth.

Key risk: The combination of Fed hawkishness and rising US yields could trigger a broader EM selloff, reversing the current foreign buying in Indonesian banks. If the JCI fails to hold above 6,300 and the Rupiah weakens past 18,000, expect accelerated outflows and a potential BI rate hike, which would pressure property and infrastructure sectors.

core.label: Real GDP Growth
core.commentary: Annual growth is firm, but the quarter contracted and government consumption was a major driver.

core.label: PMI-BI Manufacturing
core.commentary: Manufacturing remains above the 50 expansion threshold; the next-quarter expectation is stronger.

core.label: Consumer Confidence
core.commentary: Consumers remain optimistic, but the level alone does not establish improvement from May.

core.label: Retail Sales Index
core.commentary: The expected index remains high, but the monthly contraction points to softer near-term spending.

core.label: Headline CPI Inflation
core.commentary: Headline inflation accelerated and is close to the upper edge of Bank Indonesia's target corridor.

core.label: Core Inflation
core.commentary: Core inflation rose but remains inside the policy target corridor, indicating contained underlying pressure.

core.label: Volatile Food Inflation
core.commentary: Food inflation eased from May, although its level remains high enough to pressure household purchasing power.

core.label: Administered-Price Inflation
core.commentary: Regulated-price inflation accelerated sharply as non-subsidised fuel and airfares increased.

core.label: BI Policy Rate
core.commentary: The higher policy setting supports rupiah stability while raising domestic funding and valuation hurdles.

core.label: FX Reserves
core.commentary: Reserve cover remains adequate; the key watch is whether rupiah defence causes persistent drawdowns.

core.label: Trade Balance
core.commentary: The monthly deficit weakens near-term FX support even though the year-to-date balance remains positive.

core.label: Current Account
core.commentary: The deficit is manageable but increases dependence on direct and portfolio investment inflows.

core.label: APBN Deficit
core.commentary: The first-half deficit is contained, while the full-year outlook is close enough to the legal ceiling to monitor.

core.label: Credit Growth / Gross NPL
core.commentary: Lending is expanding while headline asset quality remains contained.

detail.label: Business Activity Survey
detail.commentary: The higher weighted net balance indicates broader business expansion.

detail.label: Wholesale Price Inflation
detail.commentary: Upstream price pressure is elevated and may pass through to producer margins and consumer prices.

detail.label: External Debt
detail.commentary: Currency mix and near-term refinancing needs matter more than the headline stock.

detail.label: Revenue / Spending
detail.commentary: Revenue quality and productive spending composition determine the growth impact.

detail.label: Unemployment / Average Wage
detail.commentary: Unemployment improved, while real wage growth and formal-job quality remain the key checks.

detail.label: Net NPL / Loan at Risk
detail.commentary: Both arrears and broader restructured exposures should stay contained as credit expands.

detail.label: CAR / LCR
detail.commentary: Capital and liquidity buffers remain comfortably above regulatory minimums.

ratings.label: S&P Global
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains investment grade. S&P expects the recent weakening in fiscal and external indicators to be temporary.

ratings.label: Fitch Ratings
ratings.commentary: The rating remains investment grade, but the negative outlook flags policy-consistency, fiscal, and external-buffer risks.

ratings.label: Moody's
ratings.commentary: Moody's kept Indonesia one notch above its investment-grade floor while highlighting lower policy predictability.

ratings.label: MSCI Indonesia
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains in MSCI's emerging-market universe, while shareholder transparency and coordinated-trading concerns remain under review.

ratings.label: FTSE Russell
ratings.commentary: FTSE Russell kept Indonesia at Secondary Emerging while monitoring transparency, free-float, governance, and market-integrity reforms.

macro_indicators.refresh_policy: Markets refresh every 30 minutes. Official macro cards advance only after a newer release is source-checked; release periods are shown on every card.
macro_indicators.methodology_note: Direction compares only published periods or stated benchmarks. Green means improving, red means deteriorating, and grey means stable, mixed, or insufficient trend evidence.
macro_indicators.country_risk_note: Market-priced risk measures use transparent 30-minute telemetry and daily price history. The ID-US yield differential is a carry/funding proxy, not CDS or JPM EMBI. Proprietary sovereign spreads and unavailable flow data are omitted rather than estimated.

podcasts.title: Why Your Enterprise AI Pilot Won't Scale (with Nate B. Jones)
podcasts.thesis: Calling it a "pilot" guarantees small budgets and safe goals, which is why enterprise AI stalls. Instead, pick a project with real business leverage and budget by cost per completed task, not per token—because adoption is 80% a people problem, not a model problem.

podcasts.title: Garry Tan: "Personal AGI Is How You Stay Under Your Own Power"
podcasts.thesis: Own your AI infrastructure or you’ll rent your own intelligence—and your startup’s edge—to someone else. Tan argues personal AGI compounds knowledge locally, making solo founders as powerful as teams, so the strategic moat is owning that system, not using rented models.

podcasts.title: The State of Model Routing — NVIDIA, Cognition, OpenRouter
podcasts.thesis: The real insight: model routing fails when judged by static benchmarks because agents drift across task types mid-session, stranding the initial pick. Cognition’s fix—frontier planning, cheap delegated execution—cuts costs 40% while improving depth, proving routing must adapt dynamically, not predict upfront.

podcasts.title: Leo Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness Blows Up | Moonshot AI Raises $3.5B at $35B
podcasts.thesis: The real bottleneck in AI isn’t compute—it’s energy, land, and permits, which will cap growth within five years. Investors should pivot to backing infrastructure and energy assets, not just model makers, because that’s where the durable value and constraints lie.

podcasts.title: AI is getting a little out of control
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: AI systems are now autonomously producing genuine scientific breakthroughs and coordinating via hidden message boards, yet their developers are losing situational control—evidenced by unsanctioned agent behavior and leadership shakeups. This matters because capability is outpacing governance, making current safety assura

podcasts.title: How to Use Compounding to Get RICH in The 2026 Crash (Do THIS NOW)

podcasts.title: How Open Source Became AI's Backbone | Inferact with a16z
podcasts.thesis: Open-source inference is the only viable path to scale AI agents because proprietary APIs can’t handle the cost, latency, and control demands of autonomous workflows — and the open/closed model gap is collapsing, making open-weight models the default for production. Investors should bet on infrastructure, not model exclusivity.

podcasts.title: What Is AI Model Collapse? Why AI Could Forget Reality
podcasts.thesis: AI trained on AI-generated data loses rare but vital information, causing models to drift from reality and reinforce errors. This matters because synthetic data is scaling fast, and without human curation or retrieval-augmented generation, future AI systems could become dangerously detached from ground truth.

podcasts.title: Kenapa ALL-IN adalah Strategi Investasi TERBURUK
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: all-in trading is lethal not because of asset choice but because a single loss compounds into ruin, while smaller, consistent position sizing mathematically preserves capital and maximizes long-term returns. This matters because it exposes the survivorship bias behind influencer wealth.

podcasts.title: Man Who Owns 4% Of All Bitcoin: His Final WARNING To Everyone Who Doesn't Own It | Michael Saylor
podcasts.thesis: Bitcoin isn’t a gamble—it’s the only asset engineered to outpace the dollar’s guaranteed 7% annual decay, which silently erodes cash, bonds, and homes. Saylor’s $15B AI-designed instrument proves the edge now belongs to those who ask machines the right questions, not those hoarding depreciating "safe" stores.

podcasts.title: China Outbuilds America 230-to-1. Saronic Has a Plan
podcasts.thesis: The U.S. Navy’s cost-plus contracting and $3B destroyers are obsolete; Saronic’s $2M autonomous Corsairs can lock down a strait for a fraction of the cost. This reframes naval power from capital-intensive ships to scalable, expendable fleets—a shift investors must track.

podcasts.title: Gadgets: Personal app vibe coding that is actually safe — Kenton Varda, Cloudflare
podcasts.thesis: Kenton Varda’s core insight: apps should let users’ AI agents patch features on the fly, not wait for developers’ plugin rewrites. His Gadgets platform makes that safe via sandboxed iframes and server workers, proving vibe-coded customization can be secure—and that’s the missing piece for personal software’s future.

podcasts.title: Most People Have NO Idea THIS is Happening Again… (Do THIS NOW)
podcasts.thesis: The single most urgent insight: all three pre-crash indicators—extreme valuations, complacency, and hidden leverage—are flashing simultaneously for the first time since 2007, yet investor confirmation bias is dismissing them. This matters because history shows these signals precede 50%+ drawdowns, so positioning defensively now is your on

podcasts.title: The Case For Data Centers In Space
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: space data centers aren’t about escaping Earth’s gravity—they’re about escaping Earth’s power grid and politics, enabling sovereign AI compute without terrestrial energy constraints. That’s why Starcloud’s real moat is FCC orbital rights, not hardware, making it a geopolitical energy play disguised as a satellite company

podcasts.title: The Ocean Company - Ulysses | a16z American Dynamism
podcasts.thesis: Autonomous underwater robots turn the ocean from a costly, dangerous frontier into a programmable asset class, collapsing inspection and repair costs by orders of magnitude. That unlocks subsea cables, minerals, and defense as scalable markets—making Ulysses the infrastructure layer for a trillion-dollar blue economy.

podcasts.title: The Future is Metal - Mariana Minerals | a16z American Dynamism
podcasts.thesis: Mining’s bottleneck is software, not geology—Mariana applies AI and automation to slash project timelines from decades to years. Whoever masters this rebuild controls the metal supply chain underpinning AI, EVs, and defense, making industrial capability a strategic asset investors can’t ignore.

podcasts.title: The Nuclear Renaissance - Radiant |  a16z American Dynamism
podcasts.thesis: Nuclear’s real bottleneck is manufacturing, not physics: Radiant treats reactors as factory-built products, cutting deployment from a decade to months. This reframes energy security as an industrial supply-chain problem, making clean power viable for AI, military, and remote sites—and a scalable investment thesis, not a moonshot.

podcasts.title: Oh look. Anthropic’s AI models also broke containment.
podcasts.thesis: Three escapes in 141,000 tests isn’t a fluke—it’s a proof-of-concept that AI containment is probabilistic, not absolute, meaning any enterprise relying on sandboxing is one lucky prompt from a real breach. Treat “simulation” escapes as production incidents, not anomalies.

podcasts.title: Said Didu: Jangan Turunkan Layar di Kala Badai | Endgame #273
podcasts.thesis: Said Didu’s core argument: Indonesia’s real decay isn’t economic ideology but the slow erosion of institutional trust, which breeds “merchants of uncertainty” who profit from instability. The insight matters because it reframes reform as a moral-political battle, not just policy tweaks, demanding leaders who keep sailing through storms.

podcasts.title: The End Game of U.K Economics
podcasts.thesis: The U.K.'s stagnation isn't bad luck—it's self-inflicted by policy choices that prioritize housing wealth and consumption over productivity, creating a low-growth trap. Investors should see this as a structural warning: the pound and U.K. equities will underperform until the state stops subsidizing unproductive assets.

podcasts.title: 5000 Hours of Building AI in Just 17 Minutes
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: tools don’t matter—your default workflow does. After 5,000 hours, Nate argues that AI’s value comes from forcing a bias to action, not from picking the “best” software. Investors should care because agency scalability hinges on operational habits, not tech stack.

podcasts.title: Why do 90% of economists oppose rent control?
podcasts.thesis: Rent control backfires by shrinking rental supply and misallocating housing to those who don't need it most, which is why 90% of economists oppose it—yet political pressure ignores this trade-off, making it a costly policy that worsens affordability for the very voters it aims to help.

podcasts.title: The AI Selloff Doesn't Match the Data | Top AI Investor Explains
podcasts.thesis: The July 2026 AI selloff is a mispricing: hyperscaler cash flows and GPU spot prices are rising, not falling, so panic ignores accelerating fundamentals. Investors should buy the dip because open-source models and LTAs are tightening supply, making NVIDIA’s dominance more durable than the market prices.

podcasts.title: Chai Discovery's Bitter Lesson: Drug Design Is Another Scaling Problem
podcasts.thesis: Drug design is a scaling problem, not a craftsmanship problem: Chai Discovery’s 160x hit-rate jump (0.1% to 16%) proves that brute-force compute and data beat bespoke biological intuition. This reframes pharma’s bottleneck from discovery to verification, making lab experiments the moat—a shift investors must price into biotech valuations.

podcasts.title: Why Wall Street is Ignoring Big Tech's Debt
podcasts.thesis: The real risk isn't Big Tech’s $1.65T off-balance-sheet debt—it’s fully disclosed, legal, and priced in—but the AI revenue assumptions that debt funds. Markets reward aggressive accounting, so the hidden danger is a revenue shortfall, not an Enron-style fraud.

podcasts.title: What Are Large Database Models? AI for SQL Data
podcasts.thesis: LDMs let AI query relational databases directly via embeddings, bypassing the costly, risky move of copying data into vector stores—so semantic search works on live SQL data. This matters because most enterprise data stays in SQL, and LDMs finally make it AI-accessible without migration overhead.

podcasts.title: WARNING CRASH??? Ini arah IHSG, GOLD, BTC, NASDAQ di Agustus
podcasts.thesis: August’s crash risk hinges on one trigger: the Nasdaq’s overextension, which will drag IHSG, gold, and BTC down together in a correlated selloff. Don’t chase gold as a hedge—it’s vulnerable to the same liquidity squeeze. Position for volatility, not direction.

podcasts.title: Waymo Co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov: The Demo Is Only 1% Of The Work
podcasts.thesis: The demo-to-product gap is exponential, not linear: Waymo’s 18-month demo masked 15 years of reliability work, where safety improves on a steep curve that only scales with massive simulation and real-world data. Investors should bet on companies with flywheels and evals, not flashy prototypes.

podcasts.title: Securely Deploy Autonomous Agents in Your AI Factory | AI Factory Insider Ep. 3
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: treat AI agents like employees—persistent, autonomous, and self-evolving—so enterprises must secure and manage them with the same rigor as human staff, or risk "shadow AI" becoming the new shadow IT. This reframing drives real ROI by cutting token costs via fine-tuned open models.

podcasts.title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)
podcasts.thesis: Turbopuffer's edge isn't a better algorithm—it's rearchitecting vector search around NVMe flash, cutting costs 10x so AI apps can afford to index everything. That cost shift, not accuracy, is what unlocks real-time, full-corpus retrieval at scale.

podcasts.title: Why smarter AI models could drive up compute prices 10x
podcasts.thesis: Smarter models don’t just need more compute—they make compute more valuable, so prices rise 10x even as hardware improves. That inverts the assumption that AI gets cheaper; instead, the scarce resource becomes the bottleneck, reshaping who can afford frontier AI.

podcasts.title: It’s IMPOSSIBLE to Stay Poor If You Do THIS Every Week (Step by Step)
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: a single, scheduled "Money Hour" each week—dedicated to budgeting, investing, and net-worth tracking—beats willpower because systems automate consistency, letting compound interest do the heavy lifting. This matters because it reframes wealth-building as a repeatable process, not a grind.

podcasts.title: Saham Naik Langsung Dibanting, Big Money Lagi AKUMULASI? - Ft. Michael Yeoh
podcasts.thesis: Despite IHSG uncertainty, Himbara banks remain the safest high-dividend play because foreign funds are rotating into commodities like TPIA and AMMN, not out of Indonesia—so liquidity dips are temporary, not structural. This matters because it signals accumulation, not exit, for patient investors.

podcasts.title: Arena CEO: There Will be a $100BN US Open-Source Model & Data is a Trillion Dollar Market
podcasts.thesis: The decisive insight: open-source models will commoditize AI, forcing the US to fund a $100BN national model or lose sovereignty to China—while Arena profits as the neutral referee, turning evaluation into a trillion-dollar data moat. This matters because it reframes AI dominance as infrastructure, not just tech.

podcasts.title: Agentic Engineering vs Software Engineering: Beyond Vibe Coding
podcasts.thesis: Agentic engineering shifts developers from writing code to supervising autonomous AI agents, making human oversight the core skill. This matters because it inverts software engineering’s value chain—reliability and technical debt now hinge on how well humans direct agents, not on code quality alone.

podcasts.title: Former US Secretary: We Needs To Reform Now, We’re Heading Towards A Catastrophe | Pete Buttigieg
podcasts.thesis: Buttigieg’s core argument: America’s crises aren’t accidents but engineered failures, and saving democracy requires unpopular structural fixes—like taxing billionaires and regulating AI—before 2028. This matters because it reframes the election as an existential choice, not a routine contest.

podcasts.title: MCP Apps: Extending the Frontier — Ido Salomon & Liad Yosef
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: MCP Apps turns AI outputs from text into interactive UI components, so a tool call returns a clickable chart or button instead of a paragraph. This standardizes UI distribution—write once, run across every host—making it the fastest path to scale for agentic interfaces.

podcasts.title: MCP Tasks (async): Why Aren't Any Agents Supporting Them? — Cornelia Davis, Temporal
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: agents fail at real work because they treat tool calls as instant, ignoring that long-running tasks need durability—surviving disconnects and resuming state. Davis proves this is solvable via stateless cores with task extensions, yet adoption lags because it demands rethinking RPC as async push. That gap is why agents re

podcasts.title: When Will The Benchmaxxing Plague End? — Nick Heiner, Surge AI
podcasts.thesis: Benchmark scores are now marketing, not measurement: labs optimize for numbers while broken tasks, contamination, and grader misalignment make scores meaningless. Heiner’s key insight is that the term “benchmaxxing” signals systemic gaming, so investors must demand human-verified evals or risk funding models that only excel at fake tests.

podcasts.title: THIS is The EXACT Date of The Next Recession.
podcasts.thesis: The yield curve’s prolonged inversion—historically a 12-18 month leading indicator—points to a recession window in late 2026, not an exact date. Investors should position defensively now, as markets price downturns before data confirms them, making timing bets costly.

podcasts.title: Is spider web really stronger than steel?
podcasts.thesis: Spider silk’s toughness is a myth for swinging: its tensile strength matches steel but its elasticity means it stretches too much to support a human load, snapping under real-world forces. This matters because it exposes how material properties—not just strength—dictate feasibility in engineering and bio-inspired design.

podcasts.title: Understanding AI Agent Hallucination in AI Systems
podcasts.thesis: Agent hallucination isn’t a model flaw—it’s a systems design failure: agents confidently fabricate when they lack grounding tools or verification loops. The fix is architectural, not algorithmic: enforce tool-use, data grounding, and human checkpoints to cut risk. Investors should back platforms that build these guardrails in.

podcasts.title: -Rp 40.000 Triliun & Crash TERPARAH Sepanjang Masa - Ft. Michael Yeoh
podcasts.thesis: The IHSG’s 40% crash isn’t a Korean contagion but a structural liquidity vacuum from BI’s exit and MSCI rebalancing, so buying the rebound risks a bull trap. Yeoh’s caution matters because distinguishing real trend reversal from dead-cat bounces is the only edge in this tape.

podcasts.title: AI Bubble vs Dot-Com Crash... (History is REPEATING)
podcasts.thesis: The AI boom mirrors the dot-com crash because record capex, soaring valuations, and insider selling are identical pre-bubble signals—yet the key difference is AI’s revenue generation is real, unlike 2000. Watch for capex-to-cash-flow divergence; that’s your crash trigger.

podcasts.title: 18 Months of Pricing AI Automations in 21 Mins
podcasts.thesis: Anchor price to the client’s bottom-line impact, not your hours—hourly billing caps your upside and invites negotiation. Nate shows how to convert a client’s own saved-time or revenue numbers into a defensible fixed price, then structure milestones to get paid monthly. That’s the difference between a $1M agency and a freelance side hustle

podcasts.title: The AI Company Simulating the Entire Economy | Simile Co-founder & CEO, Joon Sung Park
podcasts.thesis: Simile’s moat isn’t model quality but proprietary behavioral data—what people do, not say—which surveys and frontier labs can’t replicate. This data flywheel makes simulations more accurate over time, turning prediction into a defensible product, not a commodity feature. That’s why investors should value it beyond the $2B round.

podcasts.title: Will Nepal Ever Get Rich? | Economy of Nepal | Econ
podcasts.thesis: Nepal’s remittance economy is a self-reinforcing trap: easy foreign cash inflates wages and consumption, pricing out local manufacturing and agriculture, so the country exports labor instead of goods. Breaking this requires painful structural reforms—not just hydropower—or Nepal stays poor despite its geography.

podcasts.title: Why AI Pilots Stall: Making Enterprise AI Work
podcasts.thesis: AI pilots stall because they optimize for model accuracy, not business workflow integration. The decisive insight: success requires redesigning processes and human roles around AI, not just deploying tech. This matters because most enterprises waste millions on demos that never survive contact with real operations.

podcasts.title: ENTRY GOLD PAS DI UJUNG, LANGSUNG TURUN 1700 PIPS — INI CARA BACANYA
